explanation: Turkish etiquette sources advise against crossing your legs in a way that points the sole of your shoe toward another person, since showing a shoe sole is considered insulting. One source also states it is improper for a woman to cross her legs while sitting, though this reflects more traditional norms. In business settings, crossing legs is common, but keep feet flat and soles away from others.
local_tip: If you cross your legs, tuck your feet back and keep shoe soles pointed at the floor, never toward a colleague.
regional_note: Guidance is more conservative in traditional and religious settings; in modern Istanbul business environments, leg-crossing is widely accepted as long as soles are not directed at anyone.

also_check.note: Crossing legs is common, but showing soles or pointing feet at others is impolite.
Showing the sole of your shoe or crossing an ankle over the knee toward someone is offensive.
Crossing legs is generally acceptable, but avoid facing your foot or sole toward seniors.
